messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The failing test `test_getPackageName_Class` calls `ClassUtils.getPackageName()` with an array class `String[].class`. Looking at the `getPackageName(Class<?>)` method, it delegates to `getPackageName(String)` passing the class name.

The `getPackageName(String)` method gets the last index of the package separator `'.'` character and returns the substring before it. However, the code snippet shows some placeholder comments on lines 249-250 for "Strip array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding" but these do not appear implemented. This suggests that the array class name string encoding with leading `[` and trailing `;` characters (typical for array class names in JVM) may not be stripped off.

For example, an array class name looks like `[Ljava.lang.String;`. The last dot is found in `Ljava.lang.String;` so lastIndexOf('.') would give the index in the internal JVM class name format, which is not the normal class name, resulting in incorrect package name extraction.

The current bug report also mentions a related problem that `getShortClassName()` adds a trailing semicolon for array classes. Reviewing the `getShortClassName(Class<?>)` and `getShortClassName(String)` methods shows that they call the `String` version passing the class name, but from the snippet, there is no logic for stripping the array encoding characters around line 192 where the comment says "Handle array encoding" but actual implementation is missing.

Hence, the root cause is that the methods `getPackageName(String)` and `getShortClassName(String)` do not handle the special syntax for array class names (like leading '[' and trailing ';') properly. This leads to incorrect results when they encounter array classes.

Secondary evidence from recent similar bug reports does not seem particularly relevant as they relate to blank string validation or defensive coding with null arrays.

In summary, the bug occurs because the code does not implement the proper "strip array type encoding" logic in `getPackageName(String)` and `getShortClassName(String)` methods. They call `lastIndexOf('.')` or substring operations on the JVM internal encoded array class names, which include characters (like '[' and ';') not handled, resulting in incorrect package or class names with trailing semicolons (as described in the current bug report).

This analysis explains why the test seeing `"java.lang"` as package name for `String[].class` would currently fail or produce wrong output in affected methods.

Next step would be to suggest fixing `getPackageName(String)` and `getShortClassName(String)` methods to properly strip array encoding before extracting package or class names.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test calls ClassUtils.getPackageName(Class<?>) with an array class (e.g., String[].class), which internally calls getPackageName(String) passing the class name. The getPackageName(String) method lacks implementation to strip array encoding characters '[', 'L', and ';' from the internal JVM array class names (e.g., "[Ljava.lang.String;"). The code snippet shows placeholder comments for "Strip array encoding" but no actual stripping logic. Consequently, lastIndexOf('.') and substring operations operate on the encoded array name string, leading to incorrect package name extraction. Similarly, the current bug report identifies that getShortClassName(Class) also shows a trailing semicolon for arrays, which is confirmed by the getShortClassName(String) method lacking array encoding stripping logic despite a comment hinting it. This causes the observed bug that array types' package and short class names are incorrectly returned with extraneous characters like semicolons. The root cause is missing handling of JVM internal encoding of array class names in these methods.
Which methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getPackageName(java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.String)
